Terms Apply / Rates & Fees See Best Credit Cards If you want to travel more in 2027, there’s good news: The calendar is working in your favor next year. There are 3 federal holidays on a weekend next year, and while that may sound like a loss, it’s actually a win.
 When a federal holiday falls on a Saturday, it’s observed on the Friday before. When it falls on a Sunday, it moves to the Monday after. In 2027, that rule turns Juneteenth, Independence Day, and Christmas into 3-day weekends. In fact, the timing of federal holidays in 2027 creates 9 unique 3-day weekends.
 Most people don’t get unlimited vacation time. The calendar gets even more complicated when factoring in school breaks and work deadlines. This plan can help you stretch your PTO as far as it will go in 2027.
 Advertisement
 2027 Federal Holidays
 Most people aren’t working on most federal holidays, so you get days off without using any PTO .
 These are the federal holidays in 2027, including observed dates if applicable:
 New Year’s Day: Friday, January 1
 Martin Luther King Jr. Day: Monday, January 18
 Presidents Day: Monday, February 15
 Memorial Day: Monday, May 31
 Juneteenth: Saturday, June 19 (observed Friday, June 18)
 Independence Day: Sunday, July 4 (observed Monday, July 5)
 Labor Day: Monday, September 6
 Columbus Day/Indigenous Peoples’ Day: Monday, October 11
 Veterans Day: Thursday, November 11
 Thanksgiving: Thursday, November 25
 Christmas Day: Saturday, December 25 (observed Friday, December 24)
 There’s also a bonus worth noting: New Year’s Day 2028 falls on a Saturday, so it’s observed on Friday, December 31, 2027. That yields 12 federal holidays in 2027 for anyone who gets these days off work. You’ll definitely want to check your workplace calendar to ensure you’re aware of which days you get off.
 Let us help you maximize your PTO days for fun trips in 2027. Image credit: Alberto Riva 
 Government employees will follow the “observed” plan, giving workers a day off on a Friday or Monday when a holiday is on a weekend. Some private companies may use a different plan, while others skip certain holidays entirely. Check your employer’s 2027 holiday calendar before you book any trips — especially for anything nonrefundable.
 Use 1 Day of PTO for Every Long Weekend in 2027
 When a holiday lands on a Monday or Friday, using 1 day of PTO turns that 3-day weekend into 4 days off. The same idea applies for holidays on Thursdays if you take Friday off.
 In 2027, 6 holidays fall on a Monday : MLK Day, Presidents Day, Memorial Day, the observed day for Independence Day, Labor Day, and Columbus Day/Indigenous Peoples’ Day. For each of these, your smartest move for a 4-day weekend is using PTO on the Tuesday after, not the Friday before. Friday departures before a holiday weekend usually mean crowded airports and higher costs. Flying on Tuesday should be cheaper, and you’ll come home after most travelers are back at work.

 New Year’s Day, the observed day for Juneteenth, and the observed day for Christmas are all on Fridays in 2027. To get a 4-day weekend from each of these, you should request these days off :
 Monday, January 4
 Monday, June 21
 Monday, December 27
 For Juneteenth, you have another option: Taking off on Thursday, June 17, works equally well.
 Both Veterans Day and Thanksgiving are on Thursdays. Take Friday, November 12, and Friday, November 26, as PTO to add 2 more 4-day weekends into your 2027 calendar. If your workplace already gives the day after Thanksgiving off, you’ll save a PTO day that you can use elsewhere.
 Bottom Line: 
 Use 1 day of PTO adjacent to each of the 11 federal holidays. Doing so means you’ll get 44 days off from these 4-day weekends. That’s 4 days off for every day of vacation time you’re using. Additionally, New Year’s Day 2028 will be observed on Friday, December 31, 2027, so you’ll get a 3-day weekend to wrap up the year without using an additional PTO day.
 Advertisement
 Go Bigger: Using 4 Days of PTO for 9 Days off
 A 4-day weekend is sufficient for a short trip to Mexico or the Caribbean. If you want to go somewhere further, such as Europe or Asia, consider using more of your PTO on fewer holidays.
 Every federal holiday in 2027 can be stretched into at least a 9-day vacation by using just 4 days of PTO. Here’s an example: Around Presidents Day, you could be off work from Saturday, February 13, to Sunday, February 21 by using PTO on February 16-19.
 Mexico’s beaches can be reached easily with a 4-day weekend. Image Credit: Keri Stooksbury 
 You need a slightly different approach for Thanksgiving. Here, you’ll use PTO from Monday, November 22, through Wednesday, November 24, and another on Friday, November 26. This means using 4 PTO days, but you’ll have 9 straight days off work, running from Saturday, November 20, to Sunday, November 28.
 December is where things go from good to great. 
 With Christmas being observed on Friday, December 24, and New Year’s Day 2028 being observed on Friday, December 31, you’ll get 2 long weekends back-to-back at the tail end of 2027. Here, request paid time off from December 27 to 30 . This way, you’ll be off for 10 days, running from Friday, December 24, to Sunday, January 2, 2028. You’ll use 4 PTO days to make that happen.
 Hot Tip: 
 Still have PTO left in 2026? Christmas Day and New Year’s Day both fall on a Friday this year. Use your PTO days from December 28 to 31, giving you 10 days off in exchange. Your time off will run from Friday, December 25, to Sunday, January 3. If your company’s PTO policy is “use it or lose it,” those 4 days are worth a lot more now than they will be in January.
 Final Thoughts
 The 2027 calendar is unusually generous for anyone who wants to maximize PTO. With 3 holidays shifting from the weekend to a Friday or Monday, workers can take advantage of 9 free 3-day weekends before needing to use a single minute of paid time off.
 From there, using 1 PTO day next to each federal holiday yields 44 days off next year. However, for anyone who’d rather take fewer, longer trips, putting 4 PTO days around a single holiday makes for a nice 9- or 10-day vacation.
 We’ve only covered federal holidays here. If your employer gives you other days off, such as your birthday or local festivals, the same strategies apply. Be sure to confirm your company’s holiday calendar and PTO policies first. Not every employer has the same calendar for paid holidays.
